prose.summary: The product meets the rule of origin, so the CEPA rate can be claimed. The estimated saving is 10000.00 AED. See the checklist below for the required steps.
prose.classification: The product is classified under tariff line 32091010, Acrylic emulsion (paint). Mansha's confidence in this classification is high, but you should confirm the code with Indian customs or a customs broker before shipping.
prose.duty: Under the India-UAE CEPA, the normal (MFN) rate is 10% and the CEPA rate is 0%. The estimated saving is 10000.00 AED. Note that the CEPA rate applies only to Basic Customs Duty; other import charges such as IGST are still payable.
prose.origin: The rule of origin requires a change in tariff subheading (CTSH) and at least 40% value addition (VA). CTSH means each non‑originating input must be classified in a different 6‑digit subheading than the product, while VA is the share of the product's price that does not come from non‑originating materials, calculated on an FOB basis. The product satisfies all checks: the final manufacture was in the UAE, the operations went beyond the minimal ones, the tariff shift condition was met, and the value addition of 65% meets the 40% threshold.

notes.text: The agreement refers to box 8, but India's origin rules and certificate form use box 9; you must follow India's form when entering the country.
While UAE law requires records to be kept for at least 3 years, the CEPA requires retention for 5 years; the longer period applies to CEPA claims.
Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Indian inputs count as originating only with proof of their originating status (bilateral cumulation, Art. 3.7).
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.

Cumulation is bilateral only: originating materials from India used in production in the UAE may be counted as originating; the last production process in the UAE must still go beyond minimal operations.
The agreement says box 8, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
Fee bands are in AED and apply to the invoice value in AED; no currency conversion is done by Mansha.

Inference: a producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
Inference: SWS is charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text found).
Inference: anti-dumping and safeguard duties still apply (no exemption found).

That electronic certificates are accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system comes from CBIC Instruction 28/2022, which Mansha has read only through secondary reports (LiveLaw, taxmann), not the official text.
